title: Internal ops transparency apology draft for all-hands
content:
Context / why this exists:

- Quick note to self: refine this into two short slides + 3 minute script for Friday all-hands. This is a personal scratchpad — includes suggested apology language, Q&A, and follow-ups.
- Incident summary (short): an unexpected billing spike on hosted API between 2026-03-05 02:00 UTC and 2026-03-06 08:30 UTC caused a subset (~4%) of customers to see anomalous token charges and higher latency. Root cause: a rare edge-case in our batching logic + a monitoring threshold that missed early signal.

TL;DR for the company (one sentence):
We messed up — a serving/telemetry mismatch led to double-counted usage for a subset of requests; we fixed the systems, refunded affected customers, and are putting guardrails in place so this does not happen again.

Tone guidance (for leadership script):
- Be concise, factual, accountable.
- Avoid too much technical detail in the main remark — offer deep-dive links for folks who want more.
- Center customer impact and the remedial steps we took.
- Validate emotion: acknowledge frustration for support and sales teams who had to triage.

Suggested 90–120s all-hands script:
"Hi everyone — quick operational update. On March 5–6 we had a billing/latency incident that affected a small portion of hosted customers. The cause was an interaction between a new batching optimization and our telemetry pipeline which led to some requests being double-counted and some slower responses. We own this — we apologize to customers and to everyone internally who had to manage escalations. We have restored normal behavior, issued refunds, and pushed multiple fixes: (1) a patch to stop the double-counting, (2) an improved monitoring alert, and (3) a short-term rollback of the batching change for the impacted model variants while we complete validation. Full postmortem is linked in the ops workspace and will be posted publicly to docs by end of week. If you’re on support, sales, or CS, your leads will have talking points and the refund spreadsheet shortly. Thank you to the SRE and billing teams who worked through the weekend to resolve this."

Suggested short internal email / Slack snippet to customers (for CS draft):
"We recently identified and resolved an issue that resulted in unexpected charges for some requests between 2026-03-05 and 2026-03-06. We have refunded affected charges, implemented a fix, and are sharing a short postmortem. We’re sorry for the disruption and appreciate your patience. Please reach out to support@example.redwood.ai if you want a detailed account for your account."

Anticipated Q&A (with one-line answers):
- Q: How many customers were affected?
  A: Approximately 4% of hosted API customers saw anomalous charges or latency increases; the issue was isolated to specific model variants and traffic patterns.
- Q: Will you refund?
  A: Yes — affected charges have been refunded and CS has the list.
- Q: Is customer data or model outputs compromised?
  A: No — this was a billing/telemetry/serving accounting issue, not a data exposure.
- Q: How do we prevent regressions?
  A: Short term: revert the batching change for impacted variants and add a new metric + alert. Medium term: add a canary system that compares telemetry vs real token counters and a weekly billing reconciliation run.
- Q: How did this get past code review?
  A: The batching optimization was validated for common paths but not against an older telemetry shim used by a small platform subset; we’re improving review checklists and adding a test harness for that shim.
- Q: Will this affect our SLAs or metrics externally?
  A: No change to core SLAs; we missed early internal SLOs and are updating them.

Things to avoid saying in public remarks:
- Don’t speculate about customers’ financial impact beyond confirmed refunds.
- Don’t assign blame to named individuals — focus on process & systems.
- Avoid deep kernel/runtime specifics during the all-hands; put technical detail in the ops postmortem.

Follow-ups / owner actions (quick checklist):
- [Arun] finalize refund CSV and confirm all refunds are posted by EOD Thu (owner: Arun).
- [Leah] draft customer-facing post and pin to #customer-updates; include refund contact link (owner: Leah).
- [Diego] prepare engineering deep-dive doc + timeline for Confluence (owner: Diego).
- [Marta] short all-hands script and 2 slides; sync with CEO prep call (owner: Marta).
- [SRE] add a telemetry-vs-serving reconciliation canary job (owner: SRE team).
- [Finance] run a reconciliation report and sign off on refund totals (owner: Finance ops).

Open questions / unresolved items (notes to self):
- Do we publish a public postmortem or a redacted customer-facing summary? Need legal + comms sign-off.
- Is there a long-term product decision about batching that needs product review? Schedule meeting next week with product-hosted-api.
- Are there customers with linked contracts requiring formal notice? Work with legal to identify.

Draft talking points for support leads to use with customers:
- Reassurance: issue fixed; refunds issued; no data exposure.
- Concrete: timeframe, what we changed (reverted batching for variants X/Y, monitoring added).
- Offer: account-level walkthrough on request and contact link.

Notes to self (style & housekeeping):
- Keep the all-hands comment to one minute; longer technical Q&A can go to a follow-up session.
- Link the Confluence incident doc in the Slack message; attach the refund CSV for finance only.
- After finalizing, move this scratchpad into ops folder and rename to "incident-2026-03-billing-draft-messaging.json"

End of scratchpad.

-- Marta
(rough; will iterate with Arun/Leah/Diego)
